1	# fast-jev-compaction
     2	
     3	Claude Code plugin that replaces the compaction summary with Jev decisions:
     4	every tool call and result is scored in one fast request, stale ones are
     5	dropped or truncated, everything kept stays verbatim. Also usable as an npm
     6	library.
     7	
     8	## What and why
     9	
    10	Most context compaction asks an LLM to summarize old turns. A summary is
    11	lossy: a file path, exact error, constraint, or command can disappear even when
    12	it matters later. This library never rewrites anything. It only deletes tool
    13	calls and tool results Jev says are no longer needed, and it asks Jev while
    14	showing it the whole conversation. User and assistant text stays verbatim and
    15	in order.
    16	
    17	The repository is both an npm package (`src/`) and a Claude Code plugin
    18	(`hooks/`, `.claude-plugin/`) that uses the package to replace Claude Code's
    19	built-in compaction summary with the original messages.
    20	
    21	## How it works
    22	
    23	1. Every `tool_use` is paired with its `tool_result` by `tool_use_id`. Calls in
    24	   the first message or in the newest `preserveRecentMessages` messages are
    25	   pinned and never touched.
    26	2. The **state** sent to Jev is the whole conversation so far, oldest first,
    27	   with every tool result replaced by a short note (`ok, 4213 chars (omitted)`).
    28	   Tool inputs are included, texts are included, nothing is summarized.
    29	3. The state is fitted into `maxStateTokens` (25k by default) in stages, each
    30	   applied only if the previous one was not enough: tool inputs truncated to
    31	   1000, then 200, then 60 characters; long texts abridged to head + tail,
    32	   oldest non-pinned messages first; old non-pinned messages collapsed to a
    33	   `[… N chars omitted …]` note; old tool calls reduced to one line each
    34	   (`t12 Read file_path=src/a.ts → ok 480ch`); old call-less messages left
    35	   out; runs of old call-only messages folded into one entry. If it still
    36	   does not fit, compaction throws. Tokens are estimated without a tokenizer (a
    37	   word per six letters, half a token per digit, ~one per other symbol),
    38	   calibrated to land a little above the counts Jev reports.
    39	4. For every non-pinned call Jev gets two `noul` questions: should the **call**
    40	   stay (knowing it was made, with its input, still matters), and should the
    41	   **result** stay verbatim (its contents are still needed and re-running the
    42	   tool would not do).
    43	5. Questions are split into as many requests as needed so state plus questions
    44	   stays under `maxRequestTokens` (30k by default, under Jev's 32k request
    45	   limit). The same full state is resent with every request; requests run
    46	   concurrently and their answers are merged.
    47	6. Decisions per call, against `keepThreshold`:
    48	   - `keepResult ≥ threshold` → keep call and result;
    49	   - else `keepCall ≥ threshold` → keep the call, truncate the result to its
    50	     first `truncateHeadChars` characters plus a one-line note;
    51	   - else → remove the call together with its result.
    52	7. The message list is rebuilt: a message that loses all its content is
    53	   removed, untouched messages are returned as the same objects, and no result
    54	   is ever left without its call.
    55	
    56	Jev failures, malformed answers, a missing key, or a history that cannot be
    57	fitted throw; the caller (or the Claude Code hook) decides what to fall back to.
    58	
    59	## Install and usage
    60	
    61	```sh
    62	npm install fast-jev-compaction
    63	export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=...
    64	```
    65	
    66	```ts
    67	import { compactMessages, reductionRatio, type Message } from 'fast-jev-compaction';
    68	
    69	const transcript: Message[] = [
    70	  { role: 'user', text: 'Fix the failing test. Never edit src/generated.', toolUses: [] },
    71	  {
    72	    role: 'assistant',
    73	    text: '',
    74	    toolUses: [{ tool_use_id: 'toolu_1', tool: 'Read', input: { file_path: 'src/a.ts' } }],
    75	  },
    76	  { role: 'user', text: '', toolUses: [], toolResults: [{ tool_use_id: 'toolu_1', text: '…file…' }] },
    77	  // …
    78	];
    79	
    80	const result = await compactMessages(transcript, { preserveRecentMessages: 4 });
    81	console.log(result.messages, result.decisions, result.stats);
    82	if (reductionRatio(result) < 0.25) {
    83	  // not worth it: keep the original transcript, or summarize instead
    84	}
    85	```
    86	
    87	`Message` is a subset of Claude Code's `SessionMessage`, so a session transcript
    88	can be passed in as is.
    89	
    90	To bring your own transport, implement `JevAsker` (one `ask(state, questions)`
    91	method) and call `compact(messages, asker, options)`; `buildJevRequest` and
    92	`parseJevResponse` give you the HTTP request body and response validation.
    93	The building blocks (`collectToolCalls`, `fitState`, `batchCalls`,
    94	`decideCall`, `applyDecisions`) are exported too.
    95	
    96	`apiKey` defaults to `process.env.TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. Never commit the key or
    97	put it in a source file.
    98	
    99	## Options
   100	
   101	| Option | Default | Description |
   102	| --- | --- | --- |
   103	| `apiKey` | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` | TypeSafe API key (`compactMessages`/`JevClient`) |
   104	| `model` | `jev-latest` | Jev model name |
   105	| `baseUrl` | `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` | System One endpoint |
   106	| `fetch` | native `fetch` | Injectable fetch implementation for tests |
   107	| `goal` | last 3 user prompts | Ongoing task description included in the state |
   108	| `keepThreshold` | `0.5` | Minimum keep probability for a call or result to stay |
   109	| `preserveRecentMessages` | `6` | Newest messages never touched (the first is always kept) |
   110	| `maxStateTokens` | `25000` | Estimated token ceiling for the state |
   111	| `maxRequestTokens` | `30000` | Estimated ceiling for state plus one batch of questions |
   112	| `truncateHeadChars` | `300` | Characters of a dropped tool result retained before its note |
   113	
   114	`result.stats` reports message and character counts before and after, the
   115	per-reason decision counts, the state size in estimated tokens, which fitting
   116	stage was needed, and the number of requests.
   117	
   118	## Limitations
   119	
   120	- Only tool calls and results are candidates; text messages are never removed
   121	  or shortened in the output (they are only abridged in the state Jev sees).
   122	- Token sizes are estimates from character counts, not a tokenizer.
   123	- Calibration is at the request level; a probability is not a proof that a
   124	  result is safe to delete. The assistant can always re-run the tool.
   125	- The full state is repeated with every request, so a history near the state
   126	  ceiling costs one request per handful of questions.
   127	
   128	## Claude Code plugin
   129	
   130	The repository root is a Claude Code function-hook plugin: `hooks/fast-jev.ts`
   131	is a thin adapter that feeds `session.compact` transcripts through `src/` and
   132	falls back to Claude Code's built-in summary on errors or insufficient
   133	reduction. See [`hooks/README.md`](hooks/README.md) for configuration and the
   134	Claude Code 2.1.274 type reference.
   135	
   136	### Install in Claude Code
   137	
   138	Function hooks are an early-access Claude Code feature (2.1.274+), so the
   139	opt-in flag must be set wherever Claude Code runs, e.g. in `~/.claude/settings.json`:
   140	
   141	```json
   142	{ "env": { "CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS": "1", "TYPESAFE_API_KEY": "<your key>" } }
   143	```
   144	
   145	Then add this repository as a plugin marketplace and install the plugin,
   146	either from the shell or as slash commands inside a session:
   147	
   148	```sh
   149	claude plugin marketplace add tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction
   150	claude plugin install fast-jev-compaction@fast-jev-compaction
   151	```
   152	
   153	The install prompts for the plugin options (API key, thresholds, `truncateHeadChars`,
   154	…); leave them at their defaults to use `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` from the environment.
   155	Restart Claude Code or run `/reload-plugins`. From then on `/compact` (and
   156	auto-compaction) goes through Jev: the toast reads
   157	`fast-jev-compaction: kept N/M messages, no summary (…)` when the pruned history
   158	replaced the built-in summary, or `fallback to built-in summary (…)` when Jev
   159	could not remove enough (short sessions, or when it fails).
   160	
   161	To run from a checkout without installing: `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 claude --plugin-dir .`
   162	from the repository root. No publishing step is required; the marketplace is
   163	just the repo's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
   164	
   165	## Development
   166	
   167	```sh
   168	npm install
   169	npm run typecheck        # library + hook
   170	npm test
   171	npm run build
   172	npm run validate:plugin  # claude plugin validate
   173	TYPESAFE_API_KEY="$(cat ~/.typesafe_key)" npm run demo
   174	```
   175	
   176	The unit tests use a fake Jev and never contact TypeSafe. The demo is the live
   177	network check.
   178	
   179	## Animated demo (macOS)
   180	
   181	`demo/JevDemo` is a small native SwiftUI app that plays a scripted, dramatized
   182	version of the compaction flow inside a Claude Code-style terminal: the tool
   183	calls of a canned transcript are scored, results and calls Jev lets go turn red
   184	and collapse away, and the rest stays verbatim. It never calls the API; it
   185	exists to be screen recorded.
   186	
   187	```sh
   188	demo/JevDemo/build.sh   # builds demo/JevDemo/build/JevDemo.app and launches it
   189	```
   190	
   191	Press space in the app to replay from the start.
   192

1	# fast-jev-compaction Claude Code mod
     2	
     3	This plugin uses Claude Code function hooks to replace a compaction with the
     4	original messages, minus the tool calls and tool results Jev judged no longer
     5	needed. `hooks/fast-jev.ts` is a thin adapter: it reads the plugin options,
     6	finds the TypeSafe key, hands `session.compact` transcripts to the
     7	`fast-jev-compaction` library in `src/` (the plugin folder is the repository
     8	root, so the hook imports it directly) and maps the result back onto session
     9	messages. User and assistant text is never touched. Jev is sent the whole
    10	conversation as `state` (tool outputs replaced by a one-line note) and, for
    11	every tool call outside the pinned first and newest messages, two questions:
    12	whether the call should stay and whether its full output should stay. An
    13	item is kept when Jev's probability reaches `keepThreshold`; a dropped result
    14	is truncated to its first `truncateHeadChars` characters plus a one-line note,
    15	and a dropped call disappears with its result.
    16	
    17	The state is fitted into `maxStateTokens` in stages: tool inputs are
    18	truncated, then long texts are abridged (oldest first, pinned messages last),
    19	then old messages collapse to a `[… N chars omitted …]` note, then old tool
    20	calls shrink to one line each, then old call-less messages are left out and
    21	runs of old call-only messages fold together. Questions are split into as many requests as
    22	needed so each request (state plus questions) stays under `maxRequestTokens`;
    23	the full state is resent with every request. Token counts are estimated
    24	without a tokenizer, calibrated to land a little above what Jev reports.
    25	
    26	The mod is an early-access Claude Code function-hook module. The checked-in
    27	type reference was generated by Claude Code **2.1.274**. Enable the function
    28	hooks surface before installing or loading it:
    29	
    30	```sh
    31	export CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1
    32	export TYPESAFE_API_KEY="<your TypeSafe key>"
    33	
    34	claude plugin marketplace add tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction
    35	claude plugin install fast-jev-compaction@fast-jev-compaction
    36	```
    37	
    38	For local development:
    39	
    40	```sh
    41	CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 claude --plugin-dir .
    42	```
    43	
    44	## Configuration
    45	
    46	The plugin declares these `userConfig` values in
    47	`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:
    48	
    49	| Option | Default |
    50	| --- | ---: |
    51	| `keepThreshold` | `0.5` |
    52	| `preserveRecentMessages` | `6` |
    53	| `compactAtPercent` | `60` |
    54	| `minReductionRatio` | `0.25` |
    55	| `maxStateTokens` | `25000` |
    56	| `maxRequestTokens` | `30000` |
    57	| `truncateHeadChars` | `300` |
    58	| `model` | `jev-latest` |
    59	
    60	The TypeSafe key can be supplied as the sensitive `apiKey` plugin option or
    61	through `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. The environment variable is the recommended
    62	development setup.
    63	
    64	Every option except `apiKey`, `compactAtPercent`, `minReductionRatio` and
    65	`model` is passed straight to the library; see the root README for what they
    66	do. The `session.compact` hook runs the Jev requests concurrently. If Jev fails,
    67	the response is malformed, the key is unavailable, the history cannot be
    68	fitted into the state budget, or the estimated reduction is below
    69	`minReductionRatio`, the hook logs a fallback and delegates to Claude Code's
    70	built-in compaction. The outcome is shown as a toast and logged with the
    71	reduction, per-reason counts, state size and request count; a per-call
    72	`decisions:` line with both probabilities is logged for diagnosis. The
    73	`turn.complete` hook requests
    74	compaction when `context.percent` reaches `compactAtPercent`, with an
    75	in-flight guard.
    76	
    77	## Scope and caveat
    78	
    79	Function hooks are early access and may change between Claude Code releases.
    80	This mod uses the generated declarations from 2.1.274 in
    81	`types/claude-code.d.ts`; regenerate and review that file after a
    82	Claude Code upgrade.

input.prompt: Which endpoint and request shape does the TypeSafe SDK use on OpenRouter?

toolResults.text:
The page documents pointing the TypeSafe SDK at OpenRouter.

- Base URL: `https://openrouter.ai/api`. The SDK appends `/v1/systemone`, so requests go to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone`.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <OpenRouter API key>`. No TypeSafe account is needed.
- Model IDs: bare TypeSafe IDs are mapped: `jev-1.13` -> `typesafe/jev-1.13`, `jev-latest` -> `~typesafe/jev-latest`. Prefixed IDs are used as-is.
- Request and response format: the System One API implements TypeSafe's shapes. Requests need `model`, `state`, `questions`; responses contain `model`, `answers`, `usage`, plus OpenRouter's `id`, `provider`, and `usage.cost`.
- A separate Decisions API exists at `POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions` with its own schema; it is not the TypeSafe shape.
- `GET /api/v1/models` returns OpenRouter's model list shape, which the TypeSafe SDK rejects.

messages.text: It is `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone`. `/api/alpha/decisions` is a different API with its own schema, so the value in the docs and the test is right.
